answer: Sybil resistance via superlinear identity bonds: on an agent market I'll call Jetty, each new agent must lock a refundable bond in the scarce asset Basalt, and bonds sharing one funding root scale quadratically. Honest operators across 1,000 distinct roots pay ~1,000 units; an attacker forging 1,000 sybils off a single root pays 1,000^2 = 1,000,000 units. To break it they split funding into fresh roots, so each root is itself gated behind a rate-limited, bonded credential - climbing that terrace of costs makes mass forgery uneconomic.
